facts.text: The closest empirical literature on pre-declared stop and progression criteria comes from pilot and feasibility studies in health research; that literature supports stating progression criteria before results are known to reduce vulnerability to after-the-fact rationalization.

facts.text: Transferring health-research evidence on pre-declared stop and progression criteria to engineering is an analogy, not a proven result.

facts.text: Fallbacks should be designed before optimism pressure peaks.
facts.quote: Design fallbacks before optimism pressure peaks.

facts.text: Keeping set-based options open until a gate is a fallback option documented in practice and recommended for planning.
facts.quote: Options documented in practice and recommended here: set-based options kept open until a gate;

facts.text: A recommended fallback descoping ladder first reduces scenario classes, then narrows the operating envelope, and finally substitutes decision-support evidence for safety-case evidence.
facts.quote: a descoping ladder (fewer scenario classes, then a narrower operating envelope, then "decision-support evidence" instead of "safety-case evidence");

facts.text: A pre-defined minimum viable deliverable is a fallback option documented in practice and recommended for planning.

facts.text: Reverting to physical tests for the highest-integrity claims is a recommended fallback off-ramp documented in practice.

facts.text: Using simulation only for scenario screening while retaining physical verification as the basis for acceptance is a recommended fallback documented in practice.

facts.text: Replacing a high-fidelity sub-model with a bounded surrogate is a recommended fallback documented in practice.

facts.text: Running fewer but higher-value scenarios is a recommended fallback documented in practice.

facts.text: Assumption-based planning's hedging logic supports designing fallback options, although outcome evidence is limited.

facts.text: Loch, De Meyer and Pich (2006) and Sommer and Loch (2004) argue that plans under unforeseeable uncertainty should budget for detection, buffers and parallel trials rather than attempt prediction; this advice is expert opinion grounded in modelling studies.
facts.quote: Loch, De Meyer and Pich (2006) and Sommer and Loch (2004) argue that under unforeseeable uncertainty the plan should budget for detection, buffers and parallel trials rather than attempt prediction [126, 86].

facts.text: At each planning gate, ask what is known to be unknown and which unknown must become known before the next irreversible commitment.
facts.quote: Ask at each gate: what do we know that we do not know, and which unknown must become known before the next irreversible commitment?
